OPEN ITEM 1 -- how the pane is built today.
(a) Trigger: ase::ui::optsheet_fill (src/ase_window.tcl; bound to the Find box <KeyRelease>, the Scope combobox, Show all, and called after a row commit) ends by calling ase::ui::optsheet_preview.
(b) ase::ui::optsheet_preview calls `ase::opt_preview $sim [ase::session_state $key] {} [ase::ui::optsheet_netlist_text $key]` inside a catch.
(c) ase::ui::optsheet_netlist_text reads <rundir>/<cell>.spice WHOLE (state `rundir`, else ::netlist_dir, else $USER_CONF_DIR/simulations; never netlists, never creates a directory; {} when there is no file), then KEEPS ONLY dot cards with their `+` continuations and `.control`..`.endc` blocks, and caches that reduced text per file by {size mtime} in ase::ui::optsheet_nlcache. The unreduced text is the local `nl` and is dropped. That is the "reduced copy (or none)".
(d) ase::opt_preview (src/ase.tcl) uses netlist_text for ONE thing: ase::run_seed_line. It fills `control` as a list of {OPTION-NAME line} pairs: first, for every enabled ROW in the state's own row order, the lines of ase::analysis_suppress_lines (pre then post); then, for each TYPE of ase::preview_analysis_types, each ase::opt_scope_plan record's set line immediately followed by its restore line. Notes are a dict keyed by OPTION NAME: `leaks` -> "set for the <type> analysis and left in force for every analysis after it -- <ase::opt_leak_why>", `refused`, `suppressed`.
(e) ase::preview_analysis_types de-duplicates the types of `ase::analysis_emit_order $state 0 $sim` (operating point first), falling back to plain row order when that raises.
(f) What the pane really shows: optsheet_preview prints each slot heading (`above the analysis block`, `inside the analysis block`, `on the command line`, `in the run-directory start-up file`) then `"    [lindex $e 1]"` per entry -- THE LINE ONLY. Element 0 is never shown and there is no analysis label anywhere; notes follow under the heading `not delivered` as `<option> — <why>`. So the comment in opt_preview ("each line tagged with the analysis it belongs to") is not what is built: the tag is the option name and the window discards it. A set line and its restore line stand adjacent with no analysis between them.
(g) The deck: ase::backend::ngspice::render_deck sets `op_last 1` iff `[llength $optier_ctl] || [llength $optier_post]`. Those carriers are filled only when ase::op_gate_on [save_op_params] AND ase::op_analysis_enabled AND `ase::op_cards_for $netlist_text` is non-empty, and then by `[dict get [ase::op_tier_now $state] tier]`: a -> optier_ctl; d -> optier_post; b -> optier_write only (no reorder); default (c) -> optier_ctl only when ase::n_enabled_analyses > 1. It then walks `ase::analysis_emit_order $state $op_last <backend>` (ase::analysis_emit_rank answers 90 for `op` under op_last) and writes, per row: scope pre lines, suppress pre lines, setup, checkpoint arm, verbatim, the analysis line, ..., suppress post lines, scope post lines.
(h) "Are device requests held for this netlist text" is ase::op_cards_for / ase::op_cards_hit: EXACT string equality with the one process-wide slot `ase::op_cards` ({netlist <text> block <cards>}), written by ase::op_cards_capture / ase::op_cards_put / ase::op_cards_note_refusal at netlist time and emptied by ase::op_cards_clear at the start of every capture. ase::saves_op_cards_coming {state netlist_text} is a core proc that already spells the first three conditions ("spelled once so the two cannot drift") and render_deck calls it for its `.save all` leader. The reduced copy can only equal the captured text for a netlist that is nothing but dot cards and control blocks, so today's preview input is a MISS by construction.
(i) Tier b is reachable only through ase::op_tier_force_set (ase::op_save_tier sets `b` nowhere else, and demotes it to c when the device count exceeds ase::op_write_max_names).

OPEN ITEM 2 -- how a totals database gets stored under `op` and why some callers still see it.
(a) read_dataset() (src/save.c), typeless call (`type` NULL): the file's first plot fixes `type`. `Integrated Noise` first -> the integrated-noise arm sets type "op"; `op_asked` is 0 so `integ_is_op` stays 1 and sim_type becomes "op": the database is stored as `op` holding v(onoise_total)/v(inoise_total). A later `Operating Point` plot is then a second "op" dataset and ends the read at the variable-count mismatch.
(b) The registry key is (rawfile, sim_type). extra_rawfile() what==1, spice arm: a loop looks for an entry with the same resolved path and (type NULL or equal sim_type); a hit takes "file found: switch to it" -- NO READ, read_dataset() is not called (raw_restamp_design() runs if RAW_READ_REBIND is set). The non-spice arm has its own copy of the loop keyed on the path alone.
(c) Doors into that arm: `xschem raw read <f> [type]` (scheduler.c, 1|RAW_READ_REBIND); `xschem raw select` -> raw_select() -> the same call; the annotate_op arm (three plain calls: "op", then "dc", then "tran"); raw_case_reread() (after its own delete); the graph walkers in src/draw.c with `autoload`.
(d) `xschem raw_read` (underscore; used by load_raw, open_sub_schematic, hi_descend_newwin) is a different door: it clears the whole registry and calls read_rawfile_by_type() -> raw_read() -> read_dataset() DIRECTLY, bypassing extra_rawfile(). The database becomes xctx->raw with an empty registry and is adopted into slot 0 by the next extra_rawfile() call ("insert extra_raw_arr[0]").
(e) The annotate_op arm (xschem_cmds..., src/scheduler.c) removes (xctx->raw->rawfile, xctx->raw->sim_type) ONLY when the CURRENT database is a one-point op/dc (`allpoints == 1`), then asks extra_rawfile(1, f, "op"). So: totals current -> removed, read afresh asking op -> the Operating Point; totals loaded but NOT current -> dedupe hit -> the totals are published.
(f) Why ASE-L's own three callers were given the operating point: ase::attach_dbs runs `xschem raw clear $rawfile $sim_type` before its read; op_annot::db_attach drops every op/dc entry of the normalized path before `xschem annotate_op` (its guard G6, which is issue 0685's Tcl workaround); calc::eval_texts -> calc::et_run -> calc::et_alias reads through a private symlink/copy whenever the path is already in the registry. Three independent workarounds for one engine behaviour.
(g) Sources of a typeless read: load_raw with no type (`xschem raw_clear` then `xschem raw_read $filename`); ase::attach_dbs with an empty type (`xschem raw clear $rawfile {}` then `xschem raw read $rawfile`), reached from wviewer::attach_raw when ase::plot_sim_type answers {}; and -- not in the issue's list -- results::select with an empty sim_type (`xschem raw select $target`, typeless in raw_select()).
(h) "The database must remember how it was taken": Raw.req_sim_type (src/xschem.h) ALREADY records the type the caller asked for, NULL for unspecified -- but it is set only by extra_rawfile()'s two read arms. A database built by `xschem raw_read` (d), by raw_read_from_attr() or new_rawfile() has it NULL whatever was asked, so NULL does not mean "typeless".
(i) Who carries a database to another window: open_sub_schematic and hi_descend_newwin (src/xschem.tcl) copy NO Raw. They read `xschem raw_query rawfile` and `sim_type` of the CURRENT database, open the window, and re-read there: `op` -> `xschem annotate_op $rawfile`, anything else -> `xschem raw_read $rawfile $sim_type`, then `xschem set raw_level`. A new context starts with raw NULL and an empty registry (src/xinit.c), so the new window's read is a real read that names `op` and gets the Operating Point.

design_options.name: 1A -- the window hands the preview the unreduced netlist; the preview shows the deck's order
design_options.sketch: (1) ase::ui::optsheet_netlist_text keeps the unreduced text beside the reduced one in its cache (or a sibling proc returns it from the same cache), without changing what RS9 receives. (2) ase::ui::optsheet_preview passes it to ase::opt_preview as a NEW optional fifth argument; the reduced text keeps feeding ase::run_seed_line. (3) A side-effect-free predicate answers 'will this deck run its operating point last': ase::saves_op_cards_coming $state $text (gate, op enabled, held block for exactly this text) AND ase::n_enabled_analyses > 1 AND NOT (ase::op_tier_forced is b and the held block's device count fits ase::op_write_max_names). (4) ase::preview_analysis_types takes that answer and passes it to ase::analysis_emit_order in place of the literal 0. (5) Decide where suppression lines go (with their analysis, in deck order). WHAT IT SHOWS BEFORE A NETLIST OF THIS SESSION EXISTS: the slot misses, so the predicate answers 'first' -- which is right for Run on an existing netlist this session did not capture (that deck carries no device cards and says so), and WRONG for Netlist and Run on a default bench, which captures and then runs the operating point last. A alone has no way to say that.
design_options.risks: The predicate re-derives render_deck's switch (a second opinion) unless fenced against rendered decks over the whole matrix. ase::op_tier_now must not be called (it can start the simulator). The op_cards slot is one per process: netlisting another session's design turns this session's answer into a miss. 'Exact' means exact for the netlist ON DISK; Netlist and Run re-captures and can differ (dirty sheet -> refusal -> empty block -> op first). Per-keystroke cost of comparing the full text. RO1 must be moved. HK1 forbids ngspice words in both core procs.
